anonymous_statement.{u_1} {E : Type u_1}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (u v : E)
  (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) (i j : ℕ) :
  have G := fun x =>
    (Polynomial.aeval (inner ℝ u x)) (Polynomial.hermite i) * (Polynomial.aeval (inner ℝ v x)) (Polynomial.hermite j);
  MeasureTheory.Integrable G (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E) ∧
    ∫ (x : E), G x ∂ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E = if i = j then ↑i.factorial * inner ℝ u v ^ i else 0

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its compatible norm and Borel measurable structure. Write gamma_E for the measure defined by stdGaussian E. Concretely, if (e_k) is the standard orthonormal basis used in the definition, gamma_E is the pushforward of the finite product of real Gaussian laws gaussianReal(0,1) by (z_k) -> sum_k z_k e_k. The supplied density fixes each coordinate law as (2*pi)^(-1/2) exp(-t^2/2) dt: the mean is zero and the variance is one. Thus the Gaussian normalization is specified, not an unspecified scale. All integrals below are real Bochner/Lebesgue integrals over the whole E with respect to this same gamma_E.

Let u and v be any vectors in E with ||u||=1 and ||v||=1, and let i,j be arbitrary natural numbers, including zero. Define polynomials H_m in Z[X] by the supplied recurrence
 H_0(X)=1,
 H_(m+1)(X)=X H_m(X)-H_m'(X).
In real-valued formulas H_m(t) means evaluation at t after mapping each integer coefficient into R. This is exactly Polynomial.aeval t (Polynomial.hermite m). The recurrence gives H_1(t)=t and H_2(t)=t^2-1 and fixes the normalization; no factorial or square-root-factorial normalization is applied to H_m itself.

Define the actual real function on E
 G(x)=H_i(<u,x>) H_j(<v,x>).
Then G is integrable with respect to gamma_E and
 integral_E G(x) d gamma_E(x)
   = { i! * <u,v>^i, if i=j;
       0,             if i!=j. }

The factorial i! is a natural number cast to R, and the power is the ordinary real base <u,v> raised to the natural exponent i. It is not |<u,v>|^i, so the sign for negative overlap and odd i is retained. The zero-degree case uses 0!=1 and a^0=1, including a=0. The measure is the same standard Gaussian for both factors, so this is a shared-x mixed moment; no independence, orthogonality, or linear independence of u and v is assumed. The only vector restrictions are their two unit-norm conditions. There is no additional lower bound on dim E, although in dimension zero unit vectors do not exist. Integrability of G is part of the conclusion rather than a premise. The theorem does not separately assert that either factor belongs to L2, an orthonormal-basis completeness result, or a joint-law construction. There is no time parameter, horizon, limiting sense or existential constant.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianIntegrationByParts
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialDifferentiation
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Hermite.Gaussian
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Polynomial
import Mathlib.Tactic

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Polynomial
open scoped InnerProductSpace ENNReal

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianHermiteGram

private def hermiteR (i : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ :=
  (hermite i).map (algebraMap ℤ ℝ)

private theorem hermiteR_eval (i : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (hermiteR i).eval t = aeval t (hermite i) := by
  rw [hermiteR, Polynomial.eval_map_algebraMap]

private theorem hermiteR_succ (i : ℕ) :
    hermiteR (i+1) = X * hermiteR i - (hermiteR i).derivative := by
  unfold hermiteR
  rw [hermite_succ, Polynomial.map_sub, Polynomial.map_mul, Polynomial.map_X,
    Polynomial.derivative_map]

private theorem hermiteR_degree_le (i : ℕ) : (hermiteR i).natDegree ≤ i := by
  calc
    (hermiteR i).natDegree ≤ (hermite i).natDegree := Polynomial.natDegree_map_le
    _ = i := natDegree_hermite

private theorem hermiteR_top_iterate_derivative (i : ℕ) :
    derivative^[i] (hermiteR i) = C (i.factorial : ℝ) := by
  ext m
  cases m with
  | zero =>
      simp [coeff_iterate_derivative, hermiteR, coeff_hermite_self, Nat.descFactorial_self]
  | succ m =>
      have hz : (hermiteR i).coeff (m+1+i) = 0 :=
        coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt ((hermiteR_degree_le i).trans_lt (by omega))
      rw [coeff_iterate_derivative]
      simp [hz]

section Ridges

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

private theorem ridge_L2 (p : Polynomial ℝ) (w : E) :
    MemLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E) := by
  obtain ⟨hf, _⟩ :=
    GaussianPolynomialDifferentiation.actual_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_frechet_derivative
      (E := E) p
  exact hf w

private theorem ridge_product_integrable (p q : Polynomial ℝ) (u v : E) :
    Integrable (fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) (stdGaussian E) :=
  (ridge_L2 p u).integrable_mul (ridge_L2 q v)

private theorem hermite_adjoint_step (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1)
    (i : ℕ) (q : Polynomial ℝ) :
    (∫ x, (hermiteR (i+1)).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ * ∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.derivative.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E := by
  let p := hermiteR i
  let A : E → ℝ := fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ
  let B : E → ℝ := fun x => q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ
  let AD : E → ℝ := fun x => p.derivative.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ
  let BD : E → ℝ := fun x => q.derivative.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ
  let XB : E → ℝ := fun x => (X*p).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * B x
  let ρ := ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ
  let f : E → ℝ := fun x => A x * B x
  have hA (x : E) : HasFDerivAt A (AD x • innerSL ℝ u) x := by
    exact (p.hasDerivAt ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ).comp_hasFDerivAt x (innerSL ℝ u).hasFDerivAt
  have hB (x : E) : HasFDerivAt B (BD x • innerSL ℝ v) x := by
    exact (q.hasDerivAt ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ).comp_hasFDerivAt x (innerSL ℝ v).hasFDerivAt
  have hf (x : E) := (hA x).mul (hB x)
  have hf' : (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x u) = fun x => AD x * B x + ρ * (A x * BD x) := by
    funext x
    change fderiv ℝ (A * B) x u = _
    rw [(hf x).fderiv]
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
      innerSL_apply_apply, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hu, one_pow, mul_one,
      real_inner_comm u v, ρ]
    ring
  have hx : (fun x => ⟪x,u⟫_ℝ * f x) = XB := by
    funext x
    rw [real_inner_comm u x]
    simp only [XB, f, A, eval_mul, eval_X, mul_assoc]
  have hi : Integrable XB (stdGaussian E) := ridge_product_integrable (X*p) q u v
  have hAd : Integrable (fun x => AD x * B x) (stdGaussian E) :=
    ridge_product_integrable p.derivative q u v
  have hBd : Integrable (fun x => A x * BD x) (stdGaussian E) :=
    ridge_product_integrable p q.derivative u v
  have hs := GaussianIntegrationByParts.standard_gaussian_stein_of_integrable_fderiv f u
    (fun x => (hf x).differentiableAt)
    (ridge_product_integrable p q u v) (hx.symm ▸ hi)
    (hf'.symm ▸ (hAd.add (hBd.const_mul ρ)))
  rw [hx, hf', integral_add hAd (hBd.const_mul ρ), integral_const_mul] at hs
  calc
    _ = ∫ x, XB x - AD x * B x ∂stdGaussian E := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [hermiteR_succ]
      simp only [p, B, AD, XB, eval_sub]
      ring
    _ = _ := by
      rw [integral_sub hi hAd]
      linarith only [hs]

private theorem hermite_adjoint_iterate (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1)
    (i : ℕ) (q : Polynomial ℝ) :
    (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ ^ i * ∫ x, (derivative^[i] q).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E := by
  induction i generalizing q with
  | zero => simp [hermiteR, hermite_zero]
  | succ i ih =>
      rw [hermite_adjoint_step u v hu, ih q.derivative,
        Function.iterate_succ_apply, pow_succ]
      ring

private theorem hermite_gram_le (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1)
    (i j : ℕ) (hji : j ≤ i) :
    (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
      if i = j then (i.factorial : ℝ) * ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ ^ i else 0 := by
  rw [hermite_adjoint_iterate u v hu]
  by_cases h : i = j
  · subst j
    rw [hermiteR_top_iterate_derivative]
    simp [mul_comm]
  · have hn : (hermiteR j).natDegree < i :=
      (hermiteR_degree_le j).trans_lt (lt_of_le_of_ne hji (Ne.symm h))
    rw [iterate_derivative_eq_zero hn]
    simp [h]

end Ridges

theorem gaussian_hermite_ridge_gram
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) (i j : ℕ) :
    let G : E → ℝ := fun x =>
      Polynomial.aeval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ (Polynomial.hermite i) *
        Polynomial.aeval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ (Polynomial.hermite j)
    Integrable G (stdGaussian E) ∧
      (∫ x, G x ∂stdGaussian E) =
        if i = j then (i.factorial : ℝ) * ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ ^ i else 0 := by
  dsimp only
  simp_rw [← hermiteR_eval]
  refine ⟨ridge_product_integrable (hermiteR i) (hermiteR j) u v, ?_⟩
  rcases le_total j i with h | h
  · exact hermite_gram_le u v hu i j h
  · have hc :
        (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
        ∫ x, (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => mul_comm _ _
    rw [hc, hermite_gram_le v u hv j i h]
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst j
      simp [real_inner_comm u v]
    · simp [hij, Ne.symm hij]

#print axioms gaussian_hermite_ridge_gram

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianHermiteGram

candidate_publication_context.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Let \(u,v\in E\) satisfy \(\|u\|=\|v\|=1\), and put \(\rho=\langle u,v\rangle\). Let \(H_k\) denote the unnormalized probabilists’ Hermite polynomial, defined by \(H_0=1\) and \(H_{k+1}(t)=tH_k(t)-H_k^{\prime}(t)\). For every pair of natural degrees \(i,j\), the literal product \(x\mapsto H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)H_j(\langle v,x\rangle)\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Its integral is \(i!\rho^i\) if \(i=j\), and zero if \(i\ne j\). Both degrees can be zero, and coincident or antipodal unit directions are included.

formulae.label: Hermite products of correlated Gaussian projections

assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure; \(\gamma\) is its centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability.
\(u,v\) are actual unit vectors in the same carrier. There is no linear-independence, orthogonality or nonsingular two-dimensional density assumption.
\(i,j\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary. The polynomials have integer coefficients evaluated in \(\mathbb R\) through the canonical coefficient map.
The correlation is the actual inner product \(\rho\in[-1,1]\). Both endpoint values and zero are allowed. Product integrability is a conclusion.

\(u,v\) are actual unit vectors in the same carrier. There is no linear-independence, orthogonality or nonsingular two-dimensional density assumption.

conventions: When \(i=j=0\), the natural zeroth power gives integral one, even if \(\rho=0\). At \(u=v\), the equal-degree value is \(i!\); at \(u=-v\), it is \(i!(-1)^i\).
Dimension one is allowed. In dimension zero no unit vectors exist, so the unit-vector hypotheses are vacuous; the theorem does not create such vectors.

steps.title: Obtain integrability from polynomial Gaussian moments
steps.text: Every real polynomial ridge belongs to \(L^2(\gamma)\) by the existing Gaussian polynomial theorem. The product of any two such ridges is integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz. An extra factor \(\langle u,x\rangle\) is absorbed into the first polynomial, so the same result will supply the weighted Stein integrand.
steps.formula: p(\langle u,\cdot\rangle),q(\langle v,\cdot\rangle)\in L^2(\gamma)\ \Longrightarrow\ p(\langle u,\cdot\rangle)q(\langle v,\cdot\rangle)\in L^1(\gamma).

Each derivative term is a product of polynomial ridges, so step 1 establishes all three integrability conditions of the shared Stein theorem.
